vocabulary.meaning_en: a helping verb like can, could, might, should, will, would that changes the meaning of the main verb
vocabulary.meaning_ar: فعل ناقص / فعل مساعد شرطي (مثل can و might)

vocabulary.meaning_en: the simple form of a verb with no -s, -ed or -ing (go, help, eat)
vocabulary.example: After "will", use the base form: I will go.

vocabulary.meaning_en: able to be used in many different ways

vocabulary.example: We can modify the strength of a sentence with a modal.
There is a possibility of rain tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not sure; not known for sure
the power or skill to do something
when someone says you are allowed to do something
vocabulary.example: Can I leave early? I need your permission.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the verb form used after have (helped, done, eaten)
the tense will + have + past participle, for something finished before a future time
vocabulary.example: It will have stopped raining by noon.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say you are ready to give or do something for someone
vocabulary.example: She offered to carry my bag.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say that you will certainly do something
vocabulary.example: I promise I will call you tonight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say yes to an idea or a plan
vocabulary.example: I agree to meet you at twelve.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a plan or idea that you suggest to someone
vocabulary.example: He made a proposal, and I said yes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a skill you learned, not one you were born with
vocabulary.example: Speaking English is an acquired skill.

vocabulary.meaning_en: I don't think it is likely
vocabulary.example: I doubt I will finish today.

fine_lines.title: can vs could vs might (strength)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الأفعال الناقصة تغيّر قوة الجملة: can = قدرة أو إمكانية مؤكدة تقريبًا (100%)، could = ممكن (حوالي 60-70%)، might = احتمال أضعف (حوالي 40%).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Modals change how strong a sentence is: can = ability, almost 100%; could = possible, about 60-70%; might = weaker, about 40%.

examples.sentence: I could help you tomorrow, if I finish early.
I might help you, but I'm not sure.

fine_lines.title: will vs modal + have + PP
fine_lines.explanation_ar: will + المصدر للمستقبل. أما للماضي فنضع have + التصريف الثالث بعد الفعل الناقص: could have helped.
fine_lines.explanation_en: will + base form talks about the future. To talk about the past, put have + past participle after the modal: could have helped.

examples.sentence: I could have helped you yesterday.

fine_lines.title: can vs could (past)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: can ليس لها صيغة "have + PP" للماضي (لا نقول can have helped). الماضي من can هو could.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Can" has no past form with have + PP (not "can have helped"). The past of can is could.

examples.sentence: I could swim when I was five.

expressions.meaning_en: A short answer that promises or agrees.
expressions.example: Will you do your homework tonight? Yes, I will.

expressions.meaning_en: A short answer that shows ability.
expressions.example: Can we finish this today? Yes, we can.
Your bags look heavy. I'll help you.
Will you pass the test? I'm sure I will.

expressions.phrase: Can I go to the washroom?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنني الذهاب إلى دورة المياه؟
expressions.example: Excuse me, teacher, can I go to the washroom?

expressions.meaning_en: A strong yes to a question with will.
expressions.example: Will you call me later? Of course I will.

grammar.title: Modals use the same structure as will
grammar.explanation_ar: مع will نقول: الفاعل + will + الفعل في صيغة المصدر. الأفعال الناقصة تتبع نفس التركيب: الفاعل + فعل ناقص + المصدر. لا نضيف s ولا to ولا ing.
grammar.explanation_en: With will we say: subject + will + base verb. Modals use the same structure: subject + modal + base verb. No -s, no to, no -ing.
examples: I will go to the party.
I might go to the party.
She can speak English. (not: She can speaks)

grammar.title: Modals change the strength
grammar.explanation_ar: نستطيع تقوية will أو إضعافها بكلمات مثل I'm sure / I think / I doubt. أما الأفعال الناقصة فتغيّر القوة بنفسها: can (قوي) ← could (متوسط) ← might (ضعيف).
grammar.explanation_en: We can make will stronger or weaker with words like I'm sure / I think / I doubt. Modals change the strength by themselves: can (strong) → could (medium) → might (weak).
examples: I can win. / I could win. / I might win.

grammar.title: Modal past: modal + have + past participle
grammar.explanation_ar: كما في المستقبل التام (will have rained)، نستخدم have للربط بالماضي: could/might/would/should + have + التصريف الثالث. المعنى: كان ممكنًا في الماضي لكنه انتهى.
grammar.explanation_en: Like the future perfect (will have rained), have connects to the past: could/might/would/should + have + past participle. It means it was possible in the past, but now it is over.
examples: I could have helped you yesterday.
You should have done your homework.

grammar.title: OPAA: uses of will (offer, promise, agree, ask)
grammar.explanation_ar: will تُستخدم للعرض (I'll help you)، وللوعد (I'll do my homework)، وللموافقة على اقتراح (OK, I'll come at twelve)، وللسؤال (Will you...?).
grammar.explanation_en: Will is used to offer (I'll help you), promise (I'll do my homework), agree to a proposal (OK, I'll come at twelve) and ask (Will you...?).
examples: Offer: Your bag looks heavy. I'll carry it.
Promise: I'll finish it tonight, I promise.
Agree: OK, I'll come to your house at twelve.

grammar.title: Uses of can: ability, possibility, permission
grammar.explanation_ar: can تدل على القدرة (I can see / I can speak English)، وعلى الإمكانية في المستقبل (I can help you tomorrow)، وعلى طلب الإذن أو إعطائه (Can I go? Yes, you can).
grammar.explanation_en: Can shows ability (I can speak English), possibility, often future (I can help you tomorrow), and permission (Can I go? Yes, you can).
examples: Can I use your pen? Yes, you can.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد الفعل الناقص نستخدم المصدر بدون s أو to أو ing.
questions.explanation_en: After a modal, use the base form: no -s, to or -ing.

questions.question: Which modal is the weakest (least sure)?
I ___ helped you yesterday, but you didn't call me.
questions.explanation_en: For the past: could + have + past participle.

questions.question: "Your bags look heavy. I'll help you." Here will is used to ___.
"I doubt I will be president." How sure is the speaker?
questions.explanation_ar: I doubt تُضعف will، فالمتكلم غير متأكد.
questions.explanation_en: "I doubt" makes will weak; the speaker is not very sure.

questions.question: What is the past form of "can"?
questions.explanation_en: The past of can is could.

questions.question: "Can I go to the washroom?" Here can is used for ___.
You ___ have done your homework. Now the teacher is angry.
questions.explanation_ar: should have + PP: نصيحة متأخرة عن الماضي.
questions.explanation_en: should have + PP: advice about the past, too late now.

questions.question: In "could have helped", what does "have" do?
choices: connects the modal to the past
questions.explanation_ar: have تربط الفعل الناقص بحدث في الماضي.
questions.explanation_en: Have connects the modal to the past.

questions.question: "Why don't you come at twelve?" "OK, I'll come then." Here will is used to ___.
questions.explanation_en: The speaker agrees to the proposal.
